description: Phone link v2 X4: records on the console stream (pipe slot 2) and the pairing code. Pure codec vectors, no crypto except the PSK of each accepted code. Synthetic content.
generated_by: components/hardwareone/test/host/phone_console_vectors.cpp: production BLE_PhonePipeConsoleCore.h (writer path, PhoneReceiver, scanIngress), BLE_PhonePairCode.h and scPbkdf2
record_header: type u8 | flags u8 (bit0 MORE, bits 1-7 zero) | len u16 LE | payload
info_format: {"v":1,"fw":"<fw>","model":"<model>","line":511,"bin":489,"auth":true,"resume":false}: compact, this key order; fw and model JSON-escaped (" and \ escaped, control bytes and DEL as \u00XX, bytes >= 0x80 as ?), each cut at 64 escaped bytes, never inside an escape; an empty model is HardwareOne
rules: INFO is the first record of every console stream, and comes once
MORE is legal on TEXT and BLOB only; MORE on any other type, unknown and reserved types included, is malformed
a chain is TEXT or BLOB records with MORE ended by one without MORE (at most 4608 bytes); a record with MORE that brings the chain to 4608 is malformed (no continuation could fit)
inside an open chain only the same type or ABORT may follow; unknown types and the reserved type addressed to the receiver are skipped there as anywhere
ABORT ends an open chain (output not confirmed); with no chain open it is ignored
unknown types (0..1024 bytes, no MORE) and the reserved type addressed to the receiver (TICKET at the phone, RESUME at the P4) are skipped and counted; a known type sent the wrong way is malformed
the phone answers a malformed record with stream RESET 1; the P4 closes the stream with CLOSE 1 after its tx drains

fields.direction: p4_to_phone or phone_to_p4: the stream direction
fields.source: p4_production: bytes as the P4's record writer produces them (p4_to_phone; the phone must accept them), or the P4's production verdict on phone bytes (phone_to_p4); contract: bytes the P4 never writes and the phone's verdict under the agreed rules
fields.stream_hex: the console stream bytes from OPEN_OK, as the receiver sees them (any DATA split)
fields.records: each record the receiver examined, up to and including a malformed one: offset in stream_hex, type name, code, flags, len (from the header), payload_hex (the bytes present, up to len), verdict (deliver, skip, ignore, malformed) and fault
fields.deliveries: what the receiver hands on, in order: info, text and blob (one per whole chain), card, mirror, abort (with the cut chain's bytes so far); at the P4 command and binary. utf8 is the bytes decoded as UTF-8, or null
fields.verdict: ok or malformed; fault and fault_offset name the first malformed record (none, -1)
fields.receiver_action: none, stream_reset_1 (the phone) or close_1 (the P4)
fields.skipped: records skipped and counted (unknown or reserved types)
fields.code_vectors: input_hex/input_utf8 as typed; accepted = the input is a pairing code; canonical = the 16 symbols stored and fed to PBKDF2 (normalised_hex = their bytes); display = XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX; psk_hex = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(canonical, "HW1-PIPE-v1", 100000, 32); reason for a refusal: symbol (a byte that is no symbol after normalisation), length (not 16 symbols) or check (wrong check symbol). A refused input stays an ordinary passphrase.

code.check: symbol 16 = sum over i = 0..14 of alpha^(i+1) * v_i in GF(2^5), modulus x^5 + x^2 + 1 (0x25), alpha = x, addition = XOR; v_i = the symbol's index in the alphabet
code.entry: trim outer ASCII whitespace (09-0D, 20); ASCII uppercase; drop - and space anywhere; I and L read as 1, O as 0; any other byte (U included) means not a code
